messages:
maria: Heads up — I spotted duplicate audit events for a single RBAC role change from last night's deploy. Compliance export shows two events for the same action; one has actor="service:kms-proxy" and the other has actor=null but includes meta.orig_actor. This breaks the chain of custody for reporting. Anyone available to triage? @ajay @sophie :eyes:

maria: Example (redacted) — copying raw lines we exported:
```
{"event_id":"evt-5f8a1","actor":"service:kms-proxy","action":"role.update","target":"role:billing-admin","ts":"2026-03-19T02:12:43Z"}
{"event_id":"evt-5f8b2","actor":null,"action":"role.update","target":"role:billing-admin","ts":"2026-03-19T02:12:43Z","meta":{"orig_actor":"user:jdavis"}}
```

ajay: ack, I'll take first pass. We recently rolled the kms-proxy that injects an X-Orig-Actor header and also the rbac-service emits its own audit event. Could be a double-write in the audit pipeline or missing orig_event_id propagation.

sophie: saw the same pattern in the compliance export: group of 3 role changes where each yielded a pair like this. The second/null-actor event kills our ability to say who initiated the change in the PDF report.

chris: deploy-bot shows rbac-service and kms-proxy rolled around 2026-03-19 02:12:30-02:14:00 UTC. Link: https://internal.deploys/release/2026-03-19/rbac-kms-proxy :link:

ajay: quick triage plan:
1) replay raw kafka topic audit-raw to see which component first produced an event
2) check audit-proxy transform code for a case that creates a second event when orig headers are present
3) verify whether orig_event_id is preserved on the downstream emit
I'll start the replay now and post findings.

maria: assigning to ajay for triage. @jen (compliance) can we get a grace note in the report if we need to backfill events? Need to know acceptable options.

jen: legal/compliance — we can't sign off on un-attributable changes. If you can demonstrate the duplication is an internal pipeline artifact and provide immutable raw records showing orig_actor, we can add an annotation, but we need a remediation timeline and evidence no exfil or tamper.

chris: quick query results: `select event_id, actor, meta->>'orig_actor', ts from audit_events where target='role:billing-admin' and ts >= '2026-03-19'` returns 6 rows; 3 pairs with identical ts+action but different event_id. Grouping by (ts,action,target) shows duplicates.

ajay: found root cause in audit-proxy: when it receives a request proxied by kms-proxy it emits an enriched event, then forwards request — downstream service also emits its own event because we didn't preserve `X-Orig-Event-Id`. The pipeline dedupe step only checks event_id, so two distinct IDs pass through. Patch idea: persist orig_event_id header into downstream emitted event and have dedupe step check orig_event_id OR event_id.

sophie: can we add a regression test to the export pipeline and a pre-scan that collapses duplicates before compliance export?

ajay: yes. Plan: hotfix to audit-proxy to attach orig_event_id, add dedupe by orig_event_id in the enrich/dedupe consumer, run the kafka replay on staging, and then small prod rollout after smoke tests. ETA: hotfix -> staging in ~35m, prod in 2-3h if no regressions.

maria: please update INC-2026-045 (adding timeline + affected exports). Also export a signed proof bundle for compliance (raw kafka segments + replayed deduped output).

jen: once we have proof bundle and remediation timeline we can document in the compliance report. No exceptions until we have that evidence.

ajay: pushing patch now. I'll post PR link and a short smoke log when staging replay finishes.

maria: thanks all. Ping here when prod fixed and when exports updated. :pray:
